key_insight: Probe-space preconditioning plus larger perturbation batches makes zero-order training much faster and more stable without backpropagation.
engineering_relevance: The method cuts training memory from backprop-like levels to inference-mode levels, enabling much larger models to be trained on commodity GPUs.
method: Use 1SPSA with many probes per step and fewer overall optimization steps.
Add a single clean forward pass to form a diagonal preconditioner in probe-space (1.5-SPSA).
Combine 8-bit RNG packing, Triton fused kernels, and distributed parallelism for efficient large-model training.
evidence_signal: The authors benchmarked on six post-training datasets across Qwen3 and OPT, reporting state-of-the-art zero-order results and +3.1% SST-2 accuracy for OPT-13B in only 70 steps versus MeZO’s 100,000.
watch_item: Zero-order methods still depend on careful probe scaling and implementation efficiency, so instability or compute overhead can appear if the preconditioner and kernels are not tuned well.
paper_title: Probe-Space Preconditioning for Fast and Stable Zero-Order Training
